title: Hazard Awareness & Anticipation
whatItIs: Scan near and far, read the clues, predict what others will do and act early, so you never react at the last moment.
keyFacts: Scan near and far, use visual clues to predict hazards, then judge and prioritise them.
Drive so you can always stop within the distance you can see to be clear.
In side roads and country lanes, watch for unmarked junctions: nobody has priority.
Children looking the other way may step out without seeing you.
Residential streets: expect doors opening, cars moving off, children between parked cars.
ADI hazard perception: 14 clips, up to 5 points per hazard, pass mark 57/75.

visual.caption: Clues that a hazard is developing

items.title: Parked car starts to signal
items.text: Now it is moving away and you'd need to slow down: it has become a developing hazard.

items.title: Bus stops, ice cream vans
items.text: Pedestrians may emerge suddenly; children may run into the road. Drive slowly.

items.title: Rider looks over shoulder
items.text: They may intend to pull out, turn right or change direction: give time and space.

items.title: Large vehicle ahead
items.text: It may need extra room to turn, or to deal with a hazard you can't see: be prepared to stop and wait.

b.label: Developing hazard
points: Makes you change speed or direction

onTheTest.question: In the ADI hazard perception test, what makes a hazard 'developing'?
onTheTest.why: GOV.UK ADI part 1: something that would cause you to take action, like changing speed or direction.

onTheTest.question: A candidate reacts suddenly at the last minute to a cyclist, compromising their safety. DT1 fault?
onTheTest.why: DT1 11.11 Awareness/planning: a late reaction is a driving fault; a last-minute reaction compromising safety is serious.

traps: Clicking continuously or in a pattern scores nothing; a wrong click loses no points.
Driver aids don't replace looking: act on what is in front of you.
A signal may not have been cancelled: wait to be sure.
Eco-safe 'planning' (anticipation) is recorded on test but doesn't affect the result.
